title: CourseSource
description: A course as authored: courses/<id>/course.yaml plus its units (gameplan §7.1–7.3). Content is keyed by target language; each support language is a layer (§7.2).
$comment: v0 (Phase 2). The compiler (pipeline/src/nabu/compiler) turns this into a content-addressed bundle (bundle.schema.json).

orthographies.description: Orthographies the course teaches; the first is the default. Learners may switch (§6.3, apc).

license.description: Default SPDX license for every content item that gives none.

provenance.description: Default provenance for every content item that gives none.

facets.description: The facets the course practises (§8.5, ADR 0071); by default all of them. Exercises of any other facet are never planned: a course for a written language leaves out listen and speak, and one that shows its readings without drilling them leaves out read-script.

iPlusOne.description: Maximum new knowledge components per sentence (§7.5). Default 1.

oneOf.description: Path to a unit file, relative to course.yaml.

vocalization.description: Vowel marks for the course's words, by orthography (ADR 0053): a file next to course.yaml, or given inline. The compiler marks every word of sentences, stories and word forms with them, so the vowel-marks toggle has something to show.

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description: Who wrote it and whether it has been reviewed (§7.1). LLM authors are llm:<model>@<prompt-hash>; generated content (RBNF drills) is generated:<generator>@<version>.

title.description: Per support language (the key is a support orthography's language, e.g. en).

stories.description: Stories (gameplan §8.2 `story`, Phase 6): dialogue to read, each on a path node of kind story.

forms.description: Glossary entries: how the KC is written, per orthography (tap-to-gloss, §7.5 stage 7).

convert.description: script nodes: convert sentences between two orthographies (script-convert, §6.3).

forms.description: The sentence in each orthography of the course.

translations.description: Accept sets per support language (key: the support orthography's language, e.g. en). The first alternative is the displayed translation.

production.description: Used for L1→L2 production (needs `reverse` in every form). Default true.

SentenceForm.title: SentenceForm
SentenceForm.description: The exact surface text, plus tokens that annotate its words in order. Gaps between tokens become space and punctuation tokens.

reverse.description: Target-language accept set (§7.4) for L1→L2 production.

form.description: A form KC (form:<id>) for an inflected word.

tile.description: Tile group. Default: each word token is its own tile.

vocalized.description: This token's vowel-marked form (ADR 0053), where its surface is a homograph the course's vocalization file lists as ambiguous. Its marks removed, it must equal the surface.

DrillSpec.title: DrillSpec
DrillSpec.description: A generated drill family (§7.6). numbers: cardinals spelled out with CLDR RBNF.

ImageAsset.title: ImageAsset
ImageAsset.description: A picture of a sense KC for select-image (gameplan §8.2). No text inside the image; licensed and attributed like any other asset.

file.description: SVG, PNG or WebP, relative to course.yaml.

source.description: Where it came from (URL or description), for attribution.

CourseAudio.title: CourseAudio
CourseAudio.description: How the course gets audio (gameplan §10): synthesized from pinned readings by the listed voices, or recorded by people only. Audio belongs to the language, not an orthography: each voice reads one orthography's forms.

humanRequired.description: Refuse synthesis: only human recordings (dialects and languages without good TTS, §10.1).

AudioVoice.title: AudioVoice
AudioVoice.description: A synthetic voice of the course's cast.

speaker.description: Whose voice it is: a man's (m) or a woman's (f). A course's voices share its items at random; a sentence or story character whose grammar says who speaks goes to a voice of that gender, if the cast has one (ADR 0078). A cast of one voice reads everything.

voice.description: The provider's voice: an eSpeak NG voice name, a Piper voice id (or, with `model`, the voice's file stem in that repo), an ElevenLabs voice_id, a Cartesia voice id, or for OmniVoice and Navoiy a reference voice the audio index holds (`nabu audio cast`), whose voice every clip clones.

model.description: Hosted providers: the model, pinned to a dated snapshot where the provider has one (Cartesia "sonic-3.6-2026-08-27"; ElevenLabs "eleven_v4"). OmniVoice, Navoiy, and a Piper voice outside rhasspy/piper-voices: the Hugging Face checkpoint and its commit ("MahtaFetrat/Mana-Persian-Piper@ad9dd851…", "oddadmix/lahgtna-omnivoice-v2@55c38a61…", "aisha-org/navoiy-tts@9445f41e…"). It is the clips' recorded version.

language.description: The language code the provider takes for this course (ElevenLabs language_code, Cartesia language, OmniVoice language id), e.g. "fa", "uz", "yue", "ar". The Lahgtna checkpoint's dialect ids reuse country codes: "lb" is Lebanese Arabic there.

vowelMarks.description: With reading "text": read the text with the vowel marks the course's vocalization gives (ADR 0053) rather than as the source writes it, for a voice whose model reads them (Lahgtna reads تشكيل). A change to the vocalization then changes the clips it touches.

finalStop.description: With reading "text": end text that has no final punctuation (word cards, mostly) with the full stop of its script ("." in Latin, Cyrillic and Arabic script, "。" in Han, "।" in Devanagari; ADR 0063). Voices say a lone word more naturally as a sentence. Turning it on makes the clips it touches stale.

pronounce.description: With reading "text": a reading scheme pinned on tokens ("jyutping"). A token whose spelling does not settle its pinned reading (a polyphone, or a reading the character table lacks) is given to the provider as IPA instead of its spelling. Needs a provider that reads inline IPA (elevenlabs).

spoken.description: What the voice reads instead of an item's text (item id: text in the orthography), for a reading the text does not settle: a homograph (نه is noh "nine" in the numbers drill, na "no" elsewhere: drill.numbers.9: نُه). Vowel marks where they settle it. It must have as many words as the item, so word timings still map. The full stop of `finalStop` is added after it.

reading.description: What the voice reads: "text" (the orthography's form) or a reading scheme pinned on tokens ("jyutping").

license.description: License of the audio this voice produces: it follows the voice's own terms.

AudioCarrier.title: AudioCarrier
AudioCarrier.description: Piper: an item of at most `maxWords` words (word cards, mostly) is said at the end of this sentence and cut out at its first frame, its phonemes given at least the frames the carrier's phonemes get (ADR 0065). Some Piper models garble a lone word: their durations collapse and their reading of a short input is off, while sentences are fine.

text.description: The carrier, in the voice's orthography, ending where the item begins ("حالا این کلمه را تکرار کن، ": "now repeat this word, …").

maxWords.description: The longest item the carrier says, in words (split at spaces).

StorySource.title: StorySource
StorySource.description: A short story: lines of dialogue or narration, read in the learner's orthography, with questions along the way. Its words are glossed on tap from the course's glossary (KC forms).

node.description: The path node (kind story) the story is read at.

title.description: The title per support language (key: e.g. en).

speaker.description: The character's gender as a speaker, where the course sets it: a man (m) or a woman (f). Its lines go to a voice of the cast that matches (ADR 0078); without it, the character gets a voice of the cast at random, the same for every line of the story.

name.description: The name as written in each orthography of the course (keys: orthography ids).

StoryStep.title: StoryStep
StoryStep.description: One step of a story: a line, or a comprehension question.

speaker.description: A character id; none for narration.

forms.description: The line in every orthography of the course, tokenized like a sentence's forms.

translations.description: The line's meaning per support language: shown on request, never graded.

ask.description: Ask before showing the line. complete: choose the word missing at `gap`; arrange: build the line from its tiles, given its translation.

gap.description: complete: the KC of the missing word (exactly one word token of the line has it).

distractors.description: complete: other KCs offered, shown by their first form in the learner's orthography.

StoryChoiceSource.title: StoryChoiceSource
StoryChoiceSource.description: A comprehension question in the support language, about what has been read.

ScenarioSource.title: ScenarioSource
ScenarioSource.description: A roleplay scenario card (gameplan §13.4): who the model plays and what the learner tries to do. The model writes every line at run time, inside the learner's known vocabulary; the card holds no target-language text.

after.description: The path node a learner completes before the scenario opens.

setting.description: Where the conversation happens, per support language. Shown to the learner and sent to the model.

character.description: Who the model plays, per support language.

goal.description: What the learner tries to do, per support language.

VocalizationSource.title: VocalizationSource
VocalizationSource.description: A course's vowel marks for one orthography (ADR 0053): each word's vocalized form. A surface with several pronunciations is ambiguous: each of its tokens names its own (SourceToken.vocalized).

words.description: Surface → vocalized form (its marks removed, it is the surface).

ambiguous.description: Surfaces with more than one vocalization in the course: each token chooses.

uncertain.description: Surfaces the drafter was unsure of: a reviewer checks these first.
